utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, very much, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the transcript, it is important to know that we tried to start five minutes before. The case was then called and the Prosecutor was asked whether the Prosecution was ready to resume the examination-in-chief of the witness, Henneberry. But due to the failure of the LiveNote, there was no transcript of this first effort, first try, to start this morning. So we restarted now, and may I remind you, Mr. Henneberry, that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I apologise. There is just one point, which is also a technical point. I was informed at the end of last week that it would not be possible to correct the transcript a posteriori, that is, that technically speaking, what is going to be transcribed is what is going to be in the hearing and not post factum. So, as I indicated, the technical modifications of the transcript after the fact would not be possible. So, Mr. President, I do not see any other possibility, Mr. President, except to intervene immediately if there is a problem with the transcript. So this is a purely technical matter, and I think that I had it explained clearly to me on Thursday, the time of the last hearing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as I understand it, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if there are some mistakes in the transcript, they will be corrected overnight. If, however, a part is failing, then, of course, we should take care that the failing part is repeated one way or the other and because they cannot correct something that is not in the transcript, but if there is something in the transcript, it is a matter of names or just a matter of one or two words which appear not in the correct way in the transcript, that usually can be corrected. So if we keep this in the back of our mind and, of course, serious problems with the transcript could be reported immediately so that we could take the appropriate measures to secure that the transcript is finally correct. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ierace: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Henneberry.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last Thursday, I asked you whether you complained to senior officers of the SRK about the indiscriminate fire that you witnessed and other military observers witnessed and conveyed to you. You told us that you complained indeed to a number of senior officers, a gentleman who claimed to be your liaison officer, someone by the name of Misa, Major Indjic, and you said, "At least on one occasion, I made the same complaint to General Galic." Could you tell us, firstly, how many times did you meet General Galic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly, but it was at least three times and I suspect, based on my notes, several more times than three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the occasion or occasions on which you made those complaints to him?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: One for sure was on -- I shouldn't say "for sure," but to the best of my recollection, was on the 16th of December, prior to the official start of our meeting. The reason for our meeting was to discuss a corridor to allow civilians to leave Sarajevo. And I am fairly certain - I can't say for 100 per cent certainty but fairly certain - that prior to that meeting, I again complained that the indiscriminate shelling continued. The other occasions when I met him, shelling was a frequent discussion but I cannot say specifically what was discussed on all of those occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last Thursday, you also told us these words: "The ultimate goal as explained by Indjic and indeed General Galic was to either destroy the city or rid it of Muslims." What was the occasion on which General Galic said that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would have been the 16th December meeting. That meeting in fact is the first one I have clearly listed in my notes, although there are references to other meetings I had with him, and I recall that being a very significant meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you surprised -- what was your reaction when he said that to you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a soldier, I realised, having been there for several months, that it was beyond the realm of the feasible for the Serbian forces to be able to destroy the city. To damage it significantly, of course, but to actually destroy the city, that was not feasible for them, given their equipment and ammunition. As far as the comment about ridding the city of Muslims, that was the first time I had personally heard a very senior officer state that, and while I can't claim to be shocked, as I heard that before, it was dismaying that that statement would be made in advance of other negotiations and with the vehemence or certainty that it was given, as I recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate it was some time ago, but to the best of your recollection, can you tell us what the words were approximately that you used when you made your complaint to him about indiscriminate fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. I believe that I have to intervene, albeit a little tardily. This is a possible mistake in the French, and I am just looking. I just saw it in the text, we are talking about a very senior official, in singular, and I believe that in the French transcript it was translated as being a plural. There is a huge difference, of course, because we are talking about one person, not about a group of senior officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think this is a translation -- what I suspect to be a translation problem and that could be --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Mr. President, but the meaning is different. That's why I'm intervening. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you perhaps indicate the line where we actually had the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4.10. I don't have it on my -- on my screen any more. It is 4.10, Mr. President. I believe that it was interpreted as plural in the French transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am just trying to find the spot. I can't detect it on page 4, line 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 4.10, that is what I believe. [In English] "I had personally heard a very senior official state that," and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. It is page 4 line 10. In English, it is the -- it is not a plural, and as far as I understand, it was translated into plural. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question, Mr. Henneberry. I appreciate it was some time ago, but to the best of your recollection, can you tell us what the words were approximately that you used when you made your complaint to General Galic about indiscriminate fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The complaint became a standard complaint for many meetings with senior officials or commanders and it would have been in the context of, "The shelling continues and the targets in the city," or the "rounds," rather, "landing in the city are not always hitting military targets," words to that effect. I can't state specifically to General Galic, but that was the standard that we used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the same vein, can you tell us approximately, or at least to the best of your recollection, what the words were that he used in response?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in response to that statement from you that he said the ultimate goal was to either destroy the city or rid it of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. That response was given during the initial stages of the meeting at which the senior military observer for the entire Sarajevo was also present -- or present rather, Lieutenant-Colonel Richard Mole, from the British forces. And the issue was opening a corridor. General Galic, when that desire was offered by Colonel Mole and myself, launched into a rhetoric that had become fairly standard in that the Muslims were the aggressors, et cetera, et cetera, as we heard in fact from both sides for months, and then his response was: The ultimate goal is to destroy the city and/or rid it of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his response to your statement that -- to the effect that there were shells landing in the city, not on military targets or not on military objects?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That statement, again given frequently, was given most often - most often - met with indifference and/or comment that it is not possible to identify all targets because the Muslim forces in the city moved, and often again indifference as if it simply didn't matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you form any view as to the quality of the command structure in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that view?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally, for the most part and for most of the time, there was a recognisable and effective military hierarchy structure with the corps commander at the top, his staff advising him, various levels of command underneath that down to the section or squad level, section or squad being a handful of men. And the hierarchy was recognisable and, in effect, there were occasional lapses but, again, usually the command structure was working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you form any view of General Galic as to his professionalism or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It was perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There will be a gap in the French transcript. There was a problem with the French interpreter and I would like to ask the witness, with your leave, to repeat what he said so that the French interpreter can repeat the words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the response on the question, "Did you form any view as to the quality of the command structure of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps?"

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think so. What was not interpreted started with "and in effect."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please, Mr. Henneberry, repeat the last portion of your response which started with -- I read from the transcript: "... down to the squad level section or squad being a handful of men. And the hierarchy was recognisable and in effect..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. There were occasional lapses in the hierarchy but usually the command structure was working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please, Mr. Ierace, proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you form any view of General Galic as to his professionalism?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, sir. And after meeting with General Galic and talking with his staff, it was difficult and perhaps disturbing to reconcile that General Galic was well-respected and a very intelligent military man. There was no doubt of that. He had a commanding presence. He was respected for his military abilities and knowledge by his staff and by the military observers. The disturbing part of that was his focus on destroying the city or ridding it of Muslims, which was not in accordance with recognisable rules of conflict, rules of armed conflict. It, in fact, to be honest, was disturbing and somewhat scary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that? Could you spell that out.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to hearken back to the Nuremberg trials, where very intelligent men made decisions that were illegal and against the law and caused the death of civilians and military. And I couldn't help but thinking that General Galic, again being an intelligent military man with the respect of all, had the power within him to rid the city of the Muslims mostly, and knowing what was inside the city, I recognised and realised that that meant the death of a lot of innocents. Innocents, which I categorise as the young, the elderly, and the noncombatants, and he was determined to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other meetings do you recollect that this stage that you had with General Galic, apart from the 16th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one in later December. I could find an exact date in my notes, if you would like, but it was in late December. There was an issue of the United Nations aircraft flying outside of the authorised or recognised flight path leading into Sarajevo, especially on approach. There was a very definite flight path. I received the flight path on -- a diagram of the flight path on the map and saw personally that indeed the aircraft weren't always following that flight path. They weren't out by much, but they were out enough to cause some concern. The Serbian forces had threatened - indeed, I am told the Muslim forces as well - had threatened to shoot down any one aircraft that would not remain within the flight path boundaries. When I saw the difference on the map with what was generally known and generally agreed to and indeed being flown by the pilots, I was concerned that there would be a shoot-down, and that would be tragic for all. And I wanted to talk to General Galic, or did talk to General Galic and his staff about the differences. They were never reconciled formally in the sense that the map was not changed, the aircraft continued to fly their normal path which was outside of that which was drawn on the map, but there was no shoot-down either, not while I was there. There was shooting, aircraft were hit, but none were taken down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please consult your notes so as to check the date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the French interpretation did not have the expression "and his staff." What the witness said is exactly that and it does not appear in the French transcript. Thank you. Mr. President, the French booth is asking me to communicate the message to you. The witness is asked to speak more slowly so that the French booth can interpret everything efficiently in its entirety. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Henneberry, if the interpreters failed to translate a few words, it is usually due to the speed of speech. So may I ask you to slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the correction of Mr. Piletta-Zanin is about page 9, line 21, where in the English text, it says, "or did talk to General Galic and his staff about differences." Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I found that in my notes, if you'd like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What was the date?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 26th December, and if I may clarify, it doesn't state specifically that I did meet with him. Please acknowledge that at this point my notes were -- the situation was the same most days; they're not detailed but specifically and verbatim: "Got..."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness speak more slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Got air flight corridor agreement. Air operations agreement is different. No one seems concerned. Need to brief Galic and local commander at Lima 2." And given that on the 27th of December, the following day, it was a quiet day, I can say with some certainty that I probably met with him on the 26th or 27th or shortly thereafter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Do you recollect at this stage any specific meetings with him after that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recollect specific meetings, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times do you think you met with him altogether, approximately?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would estimate 10 or 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Henneberry, you have told us that you made observations from various Lima positions, had conversations with local commanders and senior subordinates of General Galic, where you raised concern about indiscriminate fire. You have told us that you met with General Galic on 10 or 11 occasions and you have -- you come to this experience with a military background. What was your state of mind as to whether or not General Galic had knowledge of the indiscriminate firing of shells into Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no doubt that he was aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that Major Indjic intimated to you that indeed it was part of a corps plan. Based on your observations as outlined by me in my previous question, what view, if any, do you have as to whether the indiscriminate fire was part of a corps plan?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am personally certain of that and that it was for well-calculated psychological reasons to have a psychological impact on the local populous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us a little more of what that psychological impact objective was, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: To terrorise the local civilians and Muslim forces, to make them on edge all the time, causing distress, lack of sleep, lack of will especially to carry on, lack of support for the Muslim cause, if I may use that, a standard psychological response in the sense of psychological warfare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion from mid-September until the end of your tenure there to travel around the city itself, in other words, on the Bosnian government side of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, occasionally touring with the UNMOs at the PTT and during utility repair missions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any observations of the psychological state of the civilians of Sarajevo when you did those things?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the civilian side, the impact of the psychological warfare application was working. They were indeed terrorised and on edge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any civilians say anything to you in that regard which you recollect at this stage?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to so many of them, I can't recall specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any observations as to their will to live? [Realtime transcript read in error "leave"]

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sense that their physical appearance, their emotional state, by way of body language and tone of voice and tears, it was obvious that they were distraught and wanted the situation to end. As far as will to live, I can't comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When civilians moved about the city in particular at times and in places where there was not a ceasefire, typically, did they do so by walking or by running?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: By running.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Transcript correction, Mr. President, page 13, line 3 of the English transcript, should read "will to live," that is l-i-v-e, rather than "will to leave."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Henneberry, you told us Thursday that you also complained about indiscriminate fire to approximately 8 or 9 other people on the second floor of Lukavica barracks - or Lukavica headquarters, I should say - 8 or 9 people on the second floor of senior rank. I don't recall their names or positions. When you say the second floor, you have told us that there was a flight of stairs going up from the ground level to General Galic's office and the operations room and also some restricted areas. Do you mean on that level or a different level?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean on that level, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of these people uniformed, typically?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many individuals, based on your observations, had offices on that level?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't even --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, but this is the French transcript again. I am having interpreted "individuals by officers" which is not, of course, the same thing with regards to the question asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 4 -- 14, line 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Transcript reads "approximately how many individuals, based on your observations, had offices on that level?"

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the French transcript interpreted how many "officers," which is not at all the same meaning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I now hear that a very precise translation is given by the French booth. So please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With regard to your question, I couldn't estimate what was behind the restricted door. As for the other officers, I could safely say I saw between 8 to 15 individuals at varying times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the range of responses, if any, from these 8 or 9 officers to your complaint about indiscriminate fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall they ranged from sincere concern to outright laughter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I come to that response of "sincere concern." Throughout your time at Lukavica and at various Lima positions, did you come across any individuals who struck you as being genuinely concerned about the indiscriminate fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Off the top of my head, I can think of two immediately and, in fact, three or four as I think of it, that were concerned, but they did continue with the shelling. They, in two cases, were direct -- directly in command of heavy weapons, mortars, anti-aircraft, artillery, et cetera, and in one case was in direct command of most likely a brigade and its assets, its personnel and equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to those three individuals, did their concern become apparent to you through conversation with them or by some other means?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Conversation, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the three expressly state to you that they were troubled by the indiscriminate fire, or words to that effect?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Words to that effect, yes, and also their actions, their body language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having regard to the command positions of the three of them and given that they were expressing concern or at least conveying concern to you, it would seem from your answers that their concern was in relation to orders which they were receiving from above and passing on to subordinates. Is that a correct assessment of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I did not want to interrupt my learned colleague but I have to do it because this question is referring to the previous one, and the previous one seemed to me a leading question. When we ask the question -- when the question is asked directly to know -- to confirm that they would have mentioned that they were troubled by the shooting, the random shooting, something was done which should not be done within the framework of this question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace, do you want to respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The question is constructed so as to clarify from the witness's previous few answers whether what appears to be an obvious conclusion is, in fact, correct. In other words, it is a question which, although in leading form, seeks to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied since it is already the testimony of this witness in page 15, line 4 and 5 - at least the answer to the question which we find on page 15, line 4 and 5 - where the witness confirms the concern about indiscriminate fire. So it really is a request for further clarification. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Henneberry, I can either repeat the question or you can read it on the screen in front of you before it disappears, at page 15, line 19.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can read it. I believe their concern was in two parts. One was, in my opinion, the orders that were receiving. Again, I have no doubt there was a broader corps plan based on normal military application and hierarchy and also their personal actions with regard to implementing -- correction, developing and implementing the tactical plan that followed from the corps operational plan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recollect at this stage the positions of the commanders of the heavy artillery and mortars?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones who were concerned, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Lima 3, Lima 10, while it was active, and what I believe to be a brigade commander in Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to Vogosca, on any occasion, did you actually observe civilian houses being hit by artillery or mortars or anti-aircraft fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dozens and dozens of times, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On those occasions, where was the source of fire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The source was the weapons monitored from Lima 11 and Lima 12.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of those occasions were after mid-September 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, sir, dozens and dozens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to Lima 3, did you ever observe any fire being directed to what appeared to be civilian areas in Otes?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Lima 3, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. While you were at Lima 3.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, unless my recollection on the position is incorrect. Lima 3 fired almost daily into Rajlovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From any position, did you observe artillery fire from Serb positions impacting on civilian areas in Otes?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I witnessed that the Otes offensive in fact from the Lima 3 position as it overlooked the valley, the plains, in which Otes sat, the fire coming into Otes was some of the most intense I had seen. As for observing the weapons firing into them, no, but it was a Serb offensive to take Otes, which was successful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, was that in early December, 1992, that that offensive took place?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, sir, and I could again find the exact date, if you would like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think we require the exact date for that. Thank you anyway. In relation to the brigade commander, do you recall the name of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of these observations made by you in relation to the three officers before September, that is mid-September 1992, or were they all after that date?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all after that date, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that the witness be shown some photographs. Perhaps -- I think there is a bundle which bears the Exhibit number P3449.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Henneberry, first of all, can you count the photographs of the bundle and tell me what the number is, how many there are, in other words?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have five, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you place the first of those photographs, with the assistance of the court usher, on the machine to your right and perhaps -- yes, we are zooming back now. That photograph bears the last four numbers 9095. Could you tell us, please, what it shows.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is one of the positions, a view from one of the positions at Lima 7. What is not obvious and, indeed, is not obvious from the original picture but is readable, is in this area here is the city of Sarajevo. This happened to be a misty, foggy day, and this is one of the weapons on the position during the occasion of a BBC film crew interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, Mr. Henneberry, I think you pointed to an area in the centre of the photograph, immediately above the dark hill line where there appears to be a white area with a little detail; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and if I had a map I could tell you the direction and whatnot, if you desire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is fine. In amongst the remaining photographs, is there another photograph showing Lima 7 position? Please place that on the screen. Thank you. This is a photograph which in the bottom right-hand corner shows the numbers 92, then 1, then 25. Do you appear in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir. I am the individual with the Canadian flag on the flack jacket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you also wearing a blue helmet?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the blue helmet signify, if anything?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the recognisable colour for United Nations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What size artillery piece appears in the photograph, if you recollect it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of two: It may be a 100 millimetre anti-tank gun or it may be a light artillery piece, a light Howitzer. I can't recollect specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the back of that photograph, I think there is some handwriting which has blurred. Did you place that handwriting there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since it is blurred, are you able to read it to us?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this confirms the weapon as a 100 milimetre anti-tank gun, as we were told it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Reading slowly, could you please read it out?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Me on a Serbian position in the" -- excuse me. It appears to be "hills." I am sorry, I have to read from the original here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have the original?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this one here. It's blurred on my screen. "On the eastern Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. edge of Sarajevo. In August and September, 1992, we observers lived in a tent and bunkers on this position. "After September," correction: "After several attacks, we moved to a house" something "5 kilometres away."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that word something perhaps "about"?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is, "about five kilometres away." The next paragraph or line is, "BBC film crew on position." Then the next line: "Weapon is a 100 millimetre anti-tank gun, a" -- excuse me for a moment. "... common weapon used against bunkers houses and..." I can't read the other words. One moment, please. The third line from the bottom starts: "Sarajevo is in the west in the middle of the picture. January 1993" something "date in lower right-hand corner." And I can tell you now that date is obviously incorrect. I simply didn't know how to set my camera at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you now please place on the machine, I think a photograph which shows a soldier holding a cartridge and with his left elbow resting on some military equipment. I think that bears the handwritten number, last four numbers 9288.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, before we please proceed, you identified the photograph as having in the bottom right-hand corner 92/1/25, but perhaps due to the difficulties, the witness hadn't put the right date. We have other photographs of similar positions, I presume, also bearing in the lower right-hand corner 92/1/25, so perhaps we should perhaps refer to the ERN number on the back of that photograph which is 01039092.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you -- first of all, did you take this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was taken with my camera, but I did not take it, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And indeed, how can you tell that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The local people did not have cameras and film, and this picture was, amongst others, developed with film from my camera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you appear in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I am the soldier holding the cartridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we looking at the wrong picture on the ELMO, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. That is the correct photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the gun on which you are leaning?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a twin barreled 30 millimetre Praga mobile anti-aircraft weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the approximate calibre of the round you are holding?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is 30 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts was the photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lima 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see that gun or a gun similar to it firing?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, though I can't tell you specifically where. I say "yes" because I personally saw all weapons we have accounted for firing at one time or another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see that gun or one like it firing into the city?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I take it that that is the right picture on the ELMO, since there is another picture of what seems to be this witness having his hand on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Shell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- shell, as well. Perhaps we should indicate it. The testimony was about the picture with ERN number 0103 and then 9088. Since it also bears the same date as the other picture with the shell on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I had thought I had stated that number at the outset.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I may not, Mr. President. I thought I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now place the photograph on the ELMO which shows you with your right hand at the tip of the round, and for the record, this is ERN number 01039087. Is that you in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, in the blue beret.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the weapon on which you are seated?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a towed 32 barrel multiple rocket launcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts was the photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lima 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it taken too, the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular picture was likely taken in August.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you were on the Lima side of the confrontation lines, did you ever observe the use of multiple rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the first time that you did that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably in September. I can't say specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the occasion I am thinking of, I was on position Lima 7 and was observing fire from the positions being monitored from that site - there were five of them - firing into the city. I turned around 180 degrees facing away from the city looking, I believe, to the east and observed some kilometres away a rapid twinkling of lights on a hill. I realised that it was rockets firing and, indeed, shortly thereafter, rockets went over our position at low height relative to us and somewhat beside us and landed in the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of weapon is a multiple rocket system?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is what is known as an area weapon, if I may differentiate, whereas a large calibre gun such as a sniper rifle or the Praga vehicle we saw earlier --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, again I have to interrupt, but I hear in the French interpretation that this is an air weapon. I don't think that was the witness's answer. Any weapon is not an air weapon, an aircraft weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is my recollection that the witness said it was an "area" weapon, which is not the same as an air weapon. So I take it that it is now properly translated into French. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Henneberry, you will see the first part of your answer on the screen at page 24, line 9, commencing with the words, "It is what is known as an area weapon, if I may differentiate, whereas a large calibre gun such as a sniper rifle or the Praga vehicle we saw earlier." First of all, was that correct? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, sir. I don't have it on my screen but that was my intention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you mean a large calibre gun as a sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Some sniper rifles can have a large caliber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or the Praga gun, when fired, will hit a pinpoint target, a small target, literally a couple of inches around. This multiple barrel rocket launcher is designed to have a spread pattern of tens of metres, if not hundreds of metres, depending on the type, when the shells land on the ground. It is not possible to fire the weapon and have the shells land in a very small area. They spread out in flight and then land over literally up to a kilometre square.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they designed so that the rockets all land at the same instant or at different times?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They can -- generally at different times, they can be fired. The rockets can be fired individually in banks such as eight across or rapidly one after another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If they are fired in banks, is the intention that they detonate together?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Close together, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see where in the city on that occasion the rockets landed?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say specifically. They simply landed in the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- first of all, you said that you thought that was September. Perhaps with the leave of the Defence, with the agreement of the Defence, Mr. President, since it is in the interests, I could say this to the witness: In your statement you said in relation to that occasion, these words, "On one occasion, on 23 August, 1992, which I recorded in my diary." Does it follow from those words that the incident was on the 23rd of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I have a quick look at my diary?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, you are correct. The incident I just described happened on 23 August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe multiple rocket launchers being used on other occasions after that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. On one of the gun sites, gun positions, monitored from Lima 10 and Lima 11, the sighting of those positions were such that we couldn't see into the centre of the town, so although the weapons were fired and reports from town reported -- the city rather, reported shells dropping, I did not see where the shells landed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to determine at what command level the multiple rocket launchers were positioned?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rocket -- the launcher in the picture was at a brigade headquarters. It may or may not have been used by the brigade at the brigade commander's discretion, however, these types of weapons are often gathered, collected, in significant numbers and fired based on a larger plan. Depending on the numbers and the plan, that could be at brigade level or higher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How valuable a corps asset is a multiple rocket launcher compared to, say, a field gun?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very valuable. It has a much more devastating effect and a much more -- can be fired much more easily to a target area than a number of individual pieces, such as artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How appropriate would its use be in an urban setting in terms of areas where there are civilians and military together?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inappropriate. If for no other reason than, again, the spread pattern can be a kilometre or more, if there are more weapons, as well as the, if I may use the word topography, the height of the buildings would cause some of the shells to strike buildings; others to go over them. It would be impossible to have control of the area where the rockets would land -- or to predict, rather, not have control, but predict, where the rockets would land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any sniper rifles, and by that I mean rifles which appeared to you to have a dedicated sniping purpose? Professional sniping rifles, I should say.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. A Draganov sniper rifle that was based at position Lima 7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What view, if any, was afforded from that position, that is the particular position where you saw the rifle, of the city?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- that position, that sniper rifle position, was amongst other weapons, all of which could see into houses on the outskirts, I believe the eastern -- outskirts at the eastern edge of the city, homes occupied by civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you form a view as to whether that particular rifle was attached to a particular soldiers?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. When that rifle was discussed, it was with some reverence that the soldiers on the position spoke of its lethality and the skill of the user.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not the user was permanently at that position or whether he was deployed elsewhere as well?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was also deployed elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the command structure was in relation to that sniper?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst at Lukavica barracks, did you ever hear outgoing rifle shots?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Dozens, perhaps hundreds of times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware as to whether there were sniper positions within Lukavica barracks after mid-September 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were positions for a variety of weapons and certainty positions that would be appropriate for sniper use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any heavy artillery weaponry at Lukavica barracks after mid-September 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tanks, and I believe anti-aircraft weapons, but frankly, I am a little fuzzy on the anti-aircraft part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidently, in relation to your observations of the sniper with the Draganov, were those observations made before or after mid-September 1992 or both?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Mr. President, that concludes the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. We could either start the cross-examination at this very moment and interrupt it after 10 minutes or have an early break until 10 minutes to 11.00. Is there any preference as far as the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. I think it would be good to have a break now, also, because, unfortunately, we have not yet received full translations of the diary of the witness and the reason was -- is that this was the period prior to the indictment period. But since we are talking about a systematic plan and this could be problematic for the Defence because Ms. Pilipovic and myself would like to cross-examine. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will adjourn until 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving you the opportunity to cross-examine the witness, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I would like to address one little issue with Mr. Ierace. We received a report of Dr. Kovac. Attached to the pictures were some text and I almost hate to use the word "illegible" but, to some extent, it is very badly legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suspect, Mr. President, from the copy I have seen, that it was probably a poor photocopy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know by what it was caused by, whether it was the type of printer used. If you could take care of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. So we mentioned some of these problems with translation, and Ms. Pilipovic will also cross-examine after me. Cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will interrogate you in French, if you don't mind. First of all, a general question: In your diary, I believe that's what you have before you, the notebook where you wrote notes down during your stay in Sarajevo. Is that what is before you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two things, sir. One is a verbatim typed copy of a written diary, and this brown notebook fills in some detail and/or was -- but was primarily my book.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone counsel, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can be allowed to interrupt you, Witness, this is only in order to gain time. So if I am interrupting you, this is not because I am being rude, but just trying to gain time. Thank you. Now, sir, I would like to start by asking you to tell us what you were before, your background. Before you joined the army, what was your education?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended school in the United States and joined the military right out of high school in 1979.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "high school"? Could you be more precise, please?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Grade 12. The primarily school's from kindergarten and the grades 1 through 12. And I joined actually one year after high school. I was waiting a year, working in the United States.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your school results, if you can categorize them, in terms of were you good, average, very good?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last two years, I grew up and had well above average marks. Prior to that, no, I was not a good student.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So could you perhaps define what kind of student were you, if you said you were not a good student? What kind of student were you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I paid more attention to athletics than my studies, and in the last two years, I found a better balance, athletics and studies in the last two years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you think of doing anything else apart from the army or was that a door that was suddenly opened just like that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I considered three careers: The army, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, or joining the national park service. But when I reviewed all of them, I decided the army was best for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Sir, I read with a great deal of interest your diary that you wrote in every day, and I am referring to the diary where you wrote that during this period you became a father. Do you see what I am referring to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, am I mistaken in saying that this diary was a kind of confidant for you, during this period, that you confided in this diary?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it exact that we can understand it as such that in this diary you wrote down all important events on a personal level, as well as the professional level? And what I mean, you also wrote down events that personally affected you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the first two to three months, yes, sir, but then the routine was so common that I would go several days without writing in it. But, yes, personal ideas and professional.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can see effectively, sir, that there are moments where there are no entries in this diary, that is correct. But as far as the rest of the time is concerned, we can see that what you were particularly touched by or what you were affected by, that was written down in this diary; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the written diary and the video diary, that I did, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Sir, I would like to ask you to take a document before you. This is Prosecution Exhibit 646.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order not to have too many documents, the Defence has decided to just read some passages, referring to the dates every time, and I would like to ask this witness just to answer in a word whether this is exactly what is written in the document that you edited yourself. Now I would like to make a point that all three booths have these documents before them which would facilitate matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I would be very grateful if you could just take this document that you have before you, please, and we are going directly, if you don't mind, to page 4, 4 out of 29.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, sir. I have a different document. I have my original diary here that is not numbered. It starts earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] How about if I give you the dates, is that okay?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, I will do so. [Interpretation] 2nd of August, please, second line, and I am reading: [In English] "And out continues," correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, to gain time, you can just say whether it is correct or not in this manner we can proceed more quickly. On date of 4th of August, I am reading the following: [In English] "Muslim funeral shelled. News blame Serbs, I am not sure. Both sides continue shelling each other." [Interpretation] Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Date 6th of August. [In English] Last night for me 2000 Muslims attack Hadzici." [Interpretation] Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Page 8th of August, sir. I am reading: [In English] "Serbs hit own position with 40 millimetres anti-air. Shelling was definitely a mistake as they were running a target." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the second time in reading out the passages, my friend has avoided reading some words or sentences inter-dispersed with the pieces he is reading out. I have no objection of that, but I think it appropriate that he indicates when he does that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am continuing the reading, the same day, but it is the following page: [In English] " So destroyed T-55 tank near airport with blue sign on side. Muslim poor tactics." [Interpretation] Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the 8th of August, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It should be the same day. Let me check. 9th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment please. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I think my friend has just corrected himself. It's not on the 8th. I'll look at the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the following day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. [Interpretation] On the date of the 10th of August: [In English] "Battle royal last night. Heavy artillery and machine-gun. Likely ground attack about one kilometre, 5 kilometre away." [Interpretation] Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 11th of August, that was the day that you became a father.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there are two errors in the transcript. I think because of the pronunciation, "about one kilometre, 5 kilometre away," which appears at page 34, line 23, should be "about 1.5 kilometres away." And page 34, line 11, should be "Muslim," full stop, "Poor tactics." Perhaps my friend could indicate full stops to minimise the errors. And that quote as transcribed reads: "So destroyed T-55 tank. That should be "Saw destroyed T-55 tank." That is page 34, line 10. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you agree with the correction, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I always agree, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am proceeding. I am sorry, it seems there is a page missing for the interpreters, but I cannot hand it over now. 13th of August, sir. I am very sorry. 13th of August, sir. [In English] "Moved to [inaudible] approximately 12 hours therefore near Dobrinja, six times 82 millimetres mortars on position L-4."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Due to much sniper activity, small arms firing all day." Full stop.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just the precision, you are talking here about sniper from BH army firing at your positions, that is, at you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. 15th of August. We are still talking about BH snipers and I am quoting: [In English] "Definitely shooting at us. Fortunately, trees obscured his view. Two other locals in L-4 also got close calls." Full stop.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you say "close calls," I understand that these were shots that came very close to you.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I am continuing the same date. [In English] "Rounds landed 200 millimetres away at 19.15 hours." [Interpretation] Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. 16th of August, [In English] "Full arms and sniper fire," is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I continue. [In English] I am surprised there were not more than two guys killed at L-HQ from snipers in past four days." [Interpretation] Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Incorrect, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is it incorrect?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: My actually diary that I have here, I am surprised there were not more than..." The next word is illegible, "killed at Lima headquarters from snipers in past four days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. What I have is "two guys."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I consult with my handwritten --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I in the meantime, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, see what was the exact entry on the 16th of August, because it might not be correctly in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are on the 15th of August, now, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...this moment, but just going back to line -- page 36, line 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is probably a lapsus linguae, I believe. We were talking about -- yes. No, that is correct. I am sorry. It is 16th of August. I thought you were looking at the date. No, not at all. This is a lot of small arms and sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that is at page 36, line 14, should be "lots of small arms and sniper fire." Then, meanwhile, Mr. Henneberry, you might have found what you were looking for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unfortunately, sir, that is missing from my written diary. Two sounds correct, but I don't have it in my written diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. For the transcript, this is ERN 01062842, which has this number, but let us go a bit further, please. Sir, talking about the Serbs and the positions, you said the following: "A plane with U.S. markings dropped weapons on Igman and that an UN convoy smuggled weapons to Muslims in Gorazde."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For what reason, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My friend left out two words which are the beginning of that sentence and which alter its meaning significantly. Perhaps he could repeat and read the whole sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am sorry, but I did not forget two words that would correspond to the beginning of the sentence. I said "full stop" after "four days" and I am quoting another sentence which begins, "They claim a plane with U.S." and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least, in the transcript, the words "they claim" and I heard you pronounce it, but it does not appear in the transcript. So it is not a mistake on your side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My apologise to my friend, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So at page 37, line 24 on from the second word should read: "They claim a plane with U.S. markings." That is what you read, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, 18th of August, I am reading: [In English] "Still plenty of small arms, sniper and two direct weapons 200 millimetres north." [Interpretation] Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, on 20th of August, the end of the text that I have, I am reading the following: [In English] "Electricity in house." Correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell us, sir, what was the reason that there was no electricity?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Again, a similar error, page 39, line 2, should be: "No electricity in house."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That becomes clear from the next question. So the question was why there was no electricity, Mr. Henneberry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Electricity was unreliable on both sides. I believe, at this particular house, the electricity had not yet been restored.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, sir. I am continuing on the 21st of August and I am reading from line 2, end of line 2: [In English] "At Lima headquarters HQ sniper close. He killed two Serbs yesterday at L," meaning Lukavica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That should be "While at Lima headquarters." Perhaps in the interest of avoiding these errors, Mr. President, I could respectfully suggest to my friend that he pauses before he then changes to English to read the quotes. It might give the translators a better chance of capturing all the words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps it's now another surprise, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when you change languages. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am continuing, sir, still the 21st of August. That is item 15: [In English] "Later 2 rounds of 105 millimetres landed 50 metres [Realtime transcript read in error "millimetre"] away." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is incomplete, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, is that 50 millimetre or 50 metre away? The transcript reads "millimetre" but --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, it is 50 metres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, the same problem. The transcript reads the quote beginning with the word "later." In fact, I think my friend read out, "It was 30 seconds later."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is in my recollection as well. Perhaps the suggestion of Mr. Ierace, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, was not too bad, if you just make a pause between changing into English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 22nd of August. At the end of the paragraph of the 22nd of August, I am going to now quote in English. [In English] "Two times British engineers directly targeted at L-8."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Flight injury by mortar attack British injury."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Incorrect, sir. It is "British engineer."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: British engineer?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it "flight injury" or "light injury"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slight injury, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read "slight."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 25th of August, third line, I am quoting in English. [In English] "Found out L-8 had been hit by artillery, five UNMOs hurt."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Going on to 2 lines below: [In English] "Direct 120 millimetre hit destroyed two rooms."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, same problem, again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when you change quickly from one language to another, we miss every time the first words pronounced by you in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will indicate that I will be speaking in English. We will try to make it a ritual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From the 25th of August on the 5th line, could you please repeat it? It is my recollection that it started with "house hit."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think it is "house."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "House took direct 120 millimetre hit."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It destroyed two rooms, correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going on. The last sentence, [In English] "(UN) are being directly targeted"?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you indicated that you would announce when you would change to English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am so sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat it while looking at the transcript. The last sentence was: [In English] "(UN) are being directly targeted."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, it still does not appear properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I cannot do any better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...was "us."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: "(UN) are being targeted," and that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, another topic. Since this is correct, sir, who were you targeted by?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslim forces from Mount Igman, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, is there a -- thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am interested, sir, in the 26th of August, and I am reading the following: [In English] "More heavy shelling." Is correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Still quoting: [In English] "Adjusted to UN position." "Fire adjusted to UN position."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sentence is incomplete, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the transcript, I take it that the quote was, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, just the last five words of what appears on page 43, lines 7 and 8. So the first four words, "Adjusted to UN position is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: "Fire."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it should be deleted. And it is: "Fire adjusted to UN positions..."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Only."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in the plural, "positions" not "position."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Position, singular. Right, it is singular. [Interpretation] I am going to continue with the reading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same day, sir. [In English] "We are the only targets." Is correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. I am reading your comment on the following page. On my page, it is the fourth paragraph. It is the most important paragraph for you, and it is about in the middle, and I am going to be quoting in English. [In English] "I believe that the Muslim gunners were trying to put one through the door." Is correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am just trying to find that, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the fourth paragraph on my page. Begins with the, "I volunteered to go, as L-8," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
