utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I am continuing at -- we are now on the 27th -- that is, 28th of August, and I am reading the last three lines. [In English] "They blame Serbs. Bullshit. Bullshit. They make Muslims and Croats to be innocent of any wrongdoing. News say heavy fighting when there isn't. News say light fighting when it is heavy."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Two matters. Firstly, "bullshit" is repeated. In fact, it appears only once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it was read twice by Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And secondly, I think it appropriate, in order that the context be clearer, that the previous sentence be read as well. I don't suggest that there is anything at all unfair about the selection that my learned colleague has made in relation to this quote. It is simply a matter of making it more obvious what the comment refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just going to ask the question of the witness because it is not clear, Mr. President, just to find out very briefly to what he was referring to by saying these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please, answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I object because that question does not necessarily bring out the previous sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as you know, the Chamber keeps a close eye on the context of parts of text quoted, and at the same time, tries to avoid any contamination by irrelevant parts. Since Mr. Ierace asked you to read one line in view of a better understanding of the context, would you please do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "L-1 and L-8 still unmannered due to danger. Still not safe to drive soft centred vehicles around. Got pictures of L-8 today. Read Canadian newspaper report of situation in Sarajevo." And, after that, we have the sentence: "They blame Serbs" and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that where the transcript says that L-1 and L-8, were still "unmannered," that you intended to read "unmanned."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No other objections from Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just one quick one, Mr. President. It could help if my learned friend indicated full stop or periods because, without them, the sentence is not apparent. The first period should be after the word "danger" and the second one after the word "around," again, after the word "today." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you agree, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 30th of August. First sentence, sir. [In English] "Of major attack to close airport tonight by Muslim forces." Full stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Again, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you didn't pause, so the first part of your English text is not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Told, t-o-l-d.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, sir, now I'm lost.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 30th of August, please, first sentence: [In English] "Told of major attack to close airport tonight (by Muslim forces)."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir. Sir, are you aware of the difference between the text in italics and the text not in italics, what that means, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was there any text in italics, and what would be the difference, and apart from full stops, periods? Could you also, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Gladly. I believe, for the Chamber, if I can interpret what the witness means, it is in general the parts of the text which are in italics, or some of them in italics and in brackets, are parts of the text that were added at a later date by this witness in order to clarify the text which otherwise would have been read with great difficulty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that so, sir?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The italics does not appear in my diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and could you then please indicate which part of the last line you read was in italics.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was, "by Muslim forces."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I am referring now to the 28th of September. As far as I am concerned, that is page 14 out of 29. And this is the first paragraph I am talking about after the title. You are talking about an L-12 position, and I am reading what follows, quoting in English. [In English] "This was a very isolated position about 300 metres from the front line." Full stop. "The Muslims in the surrounding hills were able to fire down into some parts of the compound." Full stop. [Interpretation] Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps Mr. Piletta-Zanin should clarify with the witness whether this indeed is an excerpt from his diary in the normal sense or whether it is a quote from another document. The document that I think Mr. Piletta-Zanin has, and I have a copy, has a heading above this section, and indeed all of it is in italics. So perhaps that should be explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Gladly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you write what I just read?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe this clarifies the matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it does not. Please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please clarify the issue. It was not a matter of whether the witness has written, but it was a matter of whether, as far as I understand, there was some other source from which it was taken, this part of his writing. If I understand you well, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That is so, Mr. President. It might expedite matters if the witness was given a copy of this document because, as I understand it, he prepared it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please clarify, and you certainly have noted the offer made by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The problem is that I don't have a copy of this document because I was going from the principal that this was the document that the witness already had before him. But as far as the italics are concerned, this is perhaps something that the witness obtained from another source. But it is him who wrote it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please tell me, Mr. Henneberry, whether the lines just quoted by Mr. Ierace [sic] are taken from any other document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, those lines do not appear in my diary. They are from another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a recommendation for a force commander's commendation and citation that I received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Does that clarify the matter, Mr. Ierace? Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am continuing sir, and I am now going on directly to the 10th of October. You mentioned on this date an evacuation from the Blazuj hospital. Do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us sir, where was the Blazuj hospital?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President again, this is not a diary entry in the normal sense and perhaps that should be explained. There is a heading for this section in the document that my friend has. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please clarify with the witness the context, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, sir, that some Ukrainian soldiers, two or three of them, Ukrainian soldiers were injured when they were targeted by Muslim soldiers or when they stepped on a -- when they were shelled or stepped on a mine?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir. That happened when their vehicle rolled over a mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that these Ukrainian soldiers were treated in the hospital that I just read the name of, the Blazuj hospital?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The Blazuj hospital being my name for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, sir, since you are referring to this hospital, could you please tell us under whose control was the Blazuj hospital?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I ask you again to slow down because the transcript in French cannot follow you. So perhaps between question and answer and then again between answer and question, a small pause. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem is the French now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...that is what I was informed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, under whose control, which army, was this hospital that we were talking about?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbian control, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I am going to read a quote, and just to be precise, it is in italics, but I am going to read it anyway since this was handed over by the Prosecution and it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, to be clear on this, the document that my friend has, on this particular page, states as follows: "6 October through 26 November no written diary entries." My friend's questions relate to the 10th of October. There is a heading that reads "10 October taken from my statement included with James De Rosenrol's [phoen] post-action report regarding casualty evacuation from Blazuj hospital dated 11 October." It is appropriate, in my submission, that when is passage is put to a witness, the document from which it comes is identified. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, was this a correct depiction of the -- of what is in the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but in the transcript there are some mistakes. But it is not very important. However, what is important, Mr. President, is that it is this document that was given by the Prosecution and it is referring to this witness. So we have got a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...to confront the witness with this part of the text of the document, but Mr. Ierace is right in asking that the -- that the -- that it is clear to the witness what is the source as written in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have this text before you because, as I am reading it, you say that I am correct. So do you have this document before you? The text that I just quoted, did you have it before you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, sir, you know the source of this document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...for us to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, could you give us the name of the doctor, of the physician who treated these three soldiers, these three UN soldiers at the Blazuj hospital?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unless it is written down here, sir, I can't recall. And I don't believe I did write it down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is not written. Was it a Serb doctor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember, since this hospital had given you its means at your disposal, did you make sure that the UN -- that the UN replaced this materiel that was used?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried, sir, but, no, I don't believe it was replaced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that it was -- you were told that the Serbs were not worthy of this materiel?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, sir. Sir, when you were on mission in this hospital, and I am talking about the same event, I will read to you what is still in italics, but it seems useful to have it read and I am now quoting in English: [In English] "There was a stack, that's the only way to describe it, a stack of about five dead children, aged around 6 or 7. I immediately turned my head away and asked the doctor what happened. He told me that they had been shelled while waiting at a bus stop." Is correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir, for this answer. Just a moment, please. According to your recollection, sir, who was it that shelled these people who were waiting for a bus?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslim forces, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, sir. We are now going on to the date of the 27th of November, and I am quoting in English now. [In English] "Reports of 15.000 (Muslim troops) from Igman led by German including Leopard tanks." Full stop.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. I am now quoting the italics which follows this passage in English: [In English] "The hill overlooks most of the downtown area and whoever held it could bring fire to bear on the downtown." Is correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I am now going on to the date of the 3rd of December that you have in your notebook, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Without identifying the hill which is identified in the previous sentence, that quote has no relevance, and I think it appropriate --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. Absolutely. I was just trying to gain time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, are we talking about the Zuc Orlic hill?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a moment, please. Sir, under whose control was this hill?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It varied, sir. It was heavily contested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period of time of your entry in your diary.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, both sides were on top of the hill, sir. I visited both sides that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later, sir?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall sir. If fluctuated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true to say that later on these hills were under the control of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to respond by saying I don't believe completely under their control, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, sir. Is it true, sir, that there were violent combats, fighting for the control of this hill in the month of December? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, sir. I am now going on to the 3rd of December, and I am quoting from the end of the first line in English now: [In English] "BBC News said Serbs shelled airport. We watched and reported Muslims shell airport from Mount Igman, Ilidza. (Again the news reports were wrong and the wrong side took the blame internationally for actions they didn't start)." Full stop. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps my friend should indicate - and I will do for him - that the last sentence was entirely in brackets and italics. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you agree, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was about to say it, but I appreciate the swiftness of Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from which position, sir, were you able to observe this?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. We are now going on to another date, 5th of December, and I am going to be quoting from the line three. I am going in English now. [In English] "Front line destruction, tanks, vehicles, buildings, animals, people."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, when you are talking about tanks, what kind of tanks or which tanks are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the one I remember best was a T-55. I don't know which side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to interrupt you. I am not asking the type or the category of the tanks. I am talking about which army. Whose tanks were they?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir. They were burned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, could they have been, technically speaking, BH army tanks?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could have, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, sir, we are going on to the 7th of December of your diary and I am going to be reading the first part of this entry, and I am now reading in English: [In English] "Heavy shelling in barracks."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, in order to avoid other problems, we are talking about Lukavic barracks?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am continuing, and this is the same line of questioning. You said, "heavy shelling." Which type of weapons was this heavy shelling fired with?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Multi-barreled rocket launcher, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the sentence that I was going to read that followed, when you indicated below that there were -- were impacts originated from what is known as Katusca. This is the weapon used by the BH forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, Katusca is relevant to a specific country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to interrupt you. I am sorry, this is my fault. Let's forget the Katusca. I am talking about the multi-barreled rocket launcher. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Do you know, sir, the Muslim forces, how many of such weapons did they have?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, sir. Did you see more than one? Several?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see any, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. I am now quoting the fourth line of the same date of the 7th of December, and I am reading as it is written, in English now. [In English] "Muslims new weapons in area." Full stop. "Called abbey" -- no, that is something else. Abbey is -- [Interpretation] I am withdrawing this last point. When you say "new weapons," what type of weapons are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The multiple rocket launchers, maybe one. Small arms weapons. New equipment as well. Possibly new artillery, but I can't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you say that on this date, the beginning of December, there were new weapons which were put at the disposal of the Muslim forces, do you know where they came from?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. From the intelligence reports, they came from the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if we are told that Sarajevo was a closed city, could you perhaps tell us, since you had intelligence reports, how did they weapons come into the city or to the surrounding area of the city? For the English transcript, that would be "where exactly" they came into the city.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where exactly, I can't confirm, sir. However, there was reportedly a tunnel under the airport, and I believe that was so. And any good soldiers can penetrate enemy lines in small numbers, and I believe that is how some got in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. I am going to go back to the hospital that we spoke of earlier and where these three Ukrainian soldiers were evacuated from.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you know about the operation that was sometimes referred to as "Operation Oxygen" and that would have included transporting gunpowder hidden in oxygen bottles and delivered to some hospitals?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I heard of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you -- when did you hear about this?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall, sir. I haven't thought of that until you just mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about it from the official circles or in the official circles?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Official, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you briefly tell us what you heard, what it was about?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, there was an accusation by the Serbian forces that under or in UN convoys, some of the items, such as oxygen bottles in this case, contained supplies destined for Muslim forces in the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is in this context that two bottles of oxygen containing gunpowder were delivered by mistake to this Serb hospital of Blazuj?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That question does not follow the answer given by the witness. The witness spoke of an accusation from Serb sources. This question asked by my learned colleague is of no assistance because it is merely an assertion by my learned colleague to the witness, an assertion made without any proper basis to this witness, given his state of knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please adapt your question --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am going to rephrase the question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear, sir, at the time that the Serbs claimed that this system was used in a general way to bring supplies to the Muslim forces; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear, sir, that the Serbs would have complained at the time that these two bottles would have arrived to them by mistake at the time to the hospital of Blazuj?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that specific, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for your answer. Now, as far as the convoys concerned that you spoke of earlier, is it true that the Serbs were complaining that some of these convoys could have been used in order to bring weapons, to smuggle weapons in?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Is it true, sir that the name of the Operation Container was also circulating in the official circles in order to denote this smuggling of weapons?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, sir. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear sir, talk of "Operation Container" in relation to the operations of weapon smuggling?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not hear an operation name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I am going to go back to the day of the 8th of December, and I am reading the first line in English now. [In English] "Heavy shelling all around." Full stop. "50 plus in barracks." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you say "50 plus," you mean more than 50 impacts on the barracks?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am now reading more or less from the middle of the paragraph, starting with "L-4," and I am quoting in English: [In English] "Had" -- "L-4 had impacts nearby. Intelligence (Serb) that use of part of a Muslim factional leader will start shelling the city." [Interpretation] Sir, could you first tell us who is this "Jusuf Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pa"? We do not have his entire last name written here.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir but, frankly, I cannot read the writing. If I may be permitted to have a look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it perhaps the name of Prazina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, sir, I have "Jusuf Pa" as an incomplete word in my written diary. I did not spell the name out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Did you hear talk of Jusuf Prazina? And could it have -- and could it have been this person?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps my friend could spell that name. And whilst I am on my feet, he has not identified the barracks and that might be useful as well, that is the barracks that received the 50 impacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I did identify the barracks, that it was Lukavica, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Lukavica barracks, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And as far as the name is concerned, I believe that P-r-a-z-i-n-a or perhaps m-a, I am not sure. I am continuing with my quote, sir, and I am reading the following sentence: [In English] "Papa side confirms firing to PTT came from P-4."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell us, where exactly was P-4?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly. It was inside Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, sir, you are writing on this day and you are telling us today that the Muslim forces shelled the PTT building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, as far as you know, did this happen on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shelling inside the city, yes, sir. Specific to the PTT, perhaps more than once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, I am now going on to the 12th of December, second line. We have here: "L-12 meeting, (artillery) impacts and snipers." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are still talking of BH army snipers, naturally, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I am now going on to the 16th of December and I am reading the following second line in English. [In English] "Meeting with Galic, interesting." Full stop. "To open corridor by fire." Full stop.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Sir, in these three lines that are not in italics - in fact, two and a half lines - do you see anything else which is referring to General Galic, apart from these nine words that I have just read to you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I am going to come back to this date a little later on. Now, 18th of December, I am reading starting from the fourth line. [In English] "Out of vehicle fluid all over. Several more rockets (German 107-millimetre surface-to-surface) very close 1 to 10 metres, Christmas tree." Full stop.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. Now, when you mentioned these weapons, these rockets, and in fact perhaps it is a missile, land-to-land 107-millimetre of German manufacture, could you perhaps tell us very briefly what it is?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told it was a 107-millimetre rocket, and in the context of what happened, it would be an anti-armoured weapon, primarily used for tanks against tanks or armoured vehicles or bunkers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you personally found this missile; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you could testify here that this is a very modern, very sophisticated weapon?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is modern, yes, sir. Not sophisticated, but modern.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, sir. Who fired on you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslim forces, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With an anti-armoured weapon?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the impression that you were deliberately targeted?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no doubt of that, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it true to say that on several occasions you had the impression or even a certainty that you were deliberately targeted by the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, why do you think that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslim forces were also angry with the United Nations. On one occasion of deliberate firing, I believe that they didn't like the reports that the UNMOs were making. And on the occasion in December, frankly, I think they just wanted to kill us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what was the reason that you would -- they would want to kill you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't like the UN as well, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think that this is a sufficient reason?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. I am going to go back to the 20th of December and I am going into English now quoting: [In English] "New weapons." Full stop. "Muslims well-equipped, especially mosques." Full stop. [Interpretation] Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I will continue with the reading. The following sentence: [In English] "The following mission stopped 1515 hours as firing (small arms). One worker hit." Full stop.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you sir. I will finish very shortly with this topic. 25th of December, sir. Is it true, sir, that for the 25th December entry, there are three and a half lines that are not in italics?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I am quoting the last sentence: [In English] "Meeting Galic/Mole/I." Full stop. "Boring. Airport road open." Full stop.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, sir. Going on from these five words that I quoted, is there anything else in relation to General Galic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The 4th of January, 1993, I am going to quote the last sentence. Did you find the entry?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last sentence in English: [In English] "Vehicle directly targeted from Mojmilo hill landed within 50 metres."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. Now, sir, this date, 4th of January 1993, the Mojmilo hill was under the control of which army at that time?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim forces, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, sir. Now, I am going to go to a completely another line of questioning before I give the floor to my co-counsel. You have confirmed that the Commander Indjic who became Colonel Indjic was the head of the secret services or the intelligent services, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I may be mistaken but I don't recollect that that was the evidence as to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say, sir, that Commander Indjic told you that he was working in the intelligence?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you testify that he was a high official or a senior officer in the area of intelligence service?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: A major, yes, sir. Major is senior officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, sir. Sir, you also said that you were friendly with Major Indjic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it true that the main task of an officer, of an intelligence officer, is to look for information, rather than give it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. If I may clarify?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please, do.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main task is to receive information, collate it, analyse it, and then give it in a fashion that is collated. If you mean was Major Indjic looking for information from me, then, yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. Otherwise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, if you finish your sentence, I would like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His function, his position, if he was in the intelligence, his main task was to look for information, have it analyzed and then have it transmitted to his superiors but not to give it to you; is that true?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as far as I could follow you, you used the word "amici in relation to Major Indjic. It appears in the transcript as being "friendly with." I do not know, but just for the sake of clarification, I would like to know for sure that the word "amici" of course which comes from "amigos" for "friend," is the same as being friendly with. I always had the feeling that you could be friendly with someone although not being friends. Could perhaps the interpreters -- perhaps could you repeat that question in the original wording and then find out that we have no misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you have -- did you have a relationship of friendship with Major Indjic or only friendly contacts which, it is true, is not the same thing?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Yes" to what?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Friendly contacts, a camaraderie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Major Indjic was for you a comrade?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Sir, would you agree with me to consider that if a person who pretends having an important position, like Major Indjic, gave you very important information on a corps plan, supposedly that would be a very important fact, would it not?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Important for a number of reasons, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Important for the reasons that would be in relation to your position as an observer, right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, for varying reasons in that capacity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, sir, if I say that it is not just important, but very important?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even fundamental, vital?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the context, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this specific context of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies, sir. I am not trying to be vague. If the information he gave was true, then it is vital. If it was to test me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you. Sir, would you agree with me to consider that this information was given to you on a specific date?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Information was given to me on several specific dates, sir. I don't recall which ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, let us say several dates, several specific dates. Sir, could you explain to me, since you said that the diary that we spoke of earlier was your confidant, what was the reason for that? Why was that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why did I write the diary, sir, or why was it my confidant?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am just going to finish my question. I am going to finish my question. What was the reason, since your diary was your confidant, you never mentioned that Major Indjic told you such things?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if these pieces of information were of a vital importance like you just said, wouldn't it be logical that at least one entry in your diary would appear in relation to this or to this effect?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be logical, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you then explain why there is nothing of that on that topic in your diary?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain why I believe that to be so, yes, sir. If that is what you would like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was tired of writing in the diary. There are plenty of vital or important points throughout the tour that I didn't put in there. I was in a sense affected by the war in that it was so commonplace and routine that I didn't want to keep putting it in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, this is due to your personal tiredness that you didn't input that vital point in your diary; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tiredness and the fact that it all seemed the same, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So I am going to go a bit further. In spite of that, you indicated, and it is obvious from your diary, that you are an able and conscientious military officer?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When you gained such information that you would have received from Major Indjic, did you immediately, as this would be your duty, make a report for your superiors?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, sir. Perhaps not immediately, but in the daily report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when would that report have been written?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The daily reports were written during the evening, sir, and transmitted at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find any trace of that report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a report every day, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will take note of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could find a suitable moment for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another five minutes and then my colleague will continue. And the moment is good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...perhaps over the one hour and a half. If we could continue for five minutes so Mr. Piletta-Zanin could conclude his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to show you a document, perhaps with the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, madam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, before we examine this document, you told us earlier, answering a Prosecution question, that General Galic told you himself that his mission or, rather, his desire was to destroy the city or to see the Muslims leave, all of them, the city. Is that what you recall to be the fact?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you alone with General Galic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, sir? Probably with Colonel Mole as well, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Colonel Mole was with you so we can go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object. My friend has not accurately reflected the evidence, the last answer of the witness, in formulating his question. My friend has said, "Very well. Colonel Mole was with you so we can go -- " In fact, the answer as to whether Colonel Mole was with the witness was: "Probably with Colonel Mole as well, sir." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you confirm, please, that for the reasons of protocol, you were not able as a major to speak to a commander who was a general or a corps general, is that true? You needed a superior rank officer with you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling me that the sergeant could have been addressing a general who is a corps commander?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I am telling you that in my position as the senior UNMO on the Serb side, I could address him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, at the time of this meeting, you said that "probably" Colonel Mole was with you. Does this probably mean any kind of certainty?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I would like to take page --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say anything, Mr. President. I don't know why there should be an objection to nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My learned colleague cut off the witness before he could complete his answer, and in any event, the question that my learned colleague asked the witness was whether "At the time of this meeting." End quote. Colonel Mole was with him. In fact, the issue is, and the earlier question from my learned colleague relates to whether Colonel Mole was with him at the time that General Galic spoke of his desire to destroy the city, et cetera. So again we have a subtle confusion, no doubt not intended, but which confuses a very important issue. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. My answer is the following: Considering the extraordinary length of the objection of Mr. Ierace, I think we should have the break now and I will continue after the break for another five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that you think that he has taken the whole five minutes you intended to use, but I will grant you a couple of minutes after the break. We will have a -- we will adjourn until 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 12.51 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I see you are on your feet. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as you promised, you will finish within five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the only point I wish to make is that I think it's important the witness be given the opportunity to finish that answer which appears at page 71, line 16. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. You told us, and I just read the first part of your answer on the page specified by Mr. Ierace -- the question was: "Now at the time of this meeting, you said that probably Colonel Mole was with you. Does this 'probably' mean any kind of certainty?" And then your answer started, at least, with "yes." Was there anything you would like to add to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe the question was in reference to when General Galic told me that he would open a city, is that correct, open a corridor? Lines previous to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If I could assist, Mr. President. It was in relation to the point in time when General Galic, according to the witness, said that his intention was to destroy the city or rid it of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And it was the occasion, the question was about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I would like to add, sir, is I am fairly certain that Colonel Mole was with me because that similar statement took us both by surprise and I am almost positive that that particular meeting with that statement, Colonel Mole was present. That is all. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is just the same, Mr. President. The Defence's position was not asked for after the objection of the Prosecution, but since things have been clarified now, am I authorised to continue? Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please take the Exhibit number D108, please. You have it before you. I would ask you to read items one, two, three, four, of this communication, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that necessary? We can all read it. If you intend to tender it as evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We would like to tender it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in this document that we have before us and it was signed by then General Mole, do you see one single sentence where this senior officer or lieutenant-colonel was complaining in any way of the facts that have just taken place just before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...make as an observation that there is no signature of anyone under it. But I don't know whether it's that what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. That is not an issue that does concern me. What does concern me is that there are clearly some preliminary questions which must be asked before Mr. Piletta-Zanin could put that question. The most obvious one is a view to establishing that this refers to the same meeting. I note that it recites the date of the 19th of December, 1992, and I think the witness's evidence is that the conversation took place at a meeting on the 16th at the same time, 1992. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please first clarify this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it true that the 19th of December, this date comes after the date of the 16th of December, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...in need of any answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps this has no meaning but okay, very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, three days after the 16th, is there in this communication a complaint of any kind by Lieutenant-Colonel Mole?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that three days later these alleged facts, Colonel Mole, that you just confirmed was with you, confirmed the following, and I am now going to quote in English: [In English] "This matter cements the already excellent relationships we enjoy. So from all UNMOs, may I express my appreciation and wish for continued mutual support in these difficult times." [Interpretation] End of quote. Now, do you see in this any negative remarks, sir?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, sir, do you know of a number of Serbs who were in Sarajevo at the time that we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians, you mean, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were only civilians, in fact, who had remained in Sarajevo as Serbs.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. An assertion by my learned colleague from the bar table as a matter of fact is, in my respectful submission, entirely out of place and it is not necessarily consistent with the evidence as I recollect it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would you please refrain next time from making these kind of statements while questioning the witness. When he asked for a clarification, it is not up to counsel to tell the witness what is the situation. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President. But the witness did understand the question. Could he answer it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am aware of both civilians and military Serbians in the city of Sarajevo, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was about the number, how many people were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In your question, you wanted to exclude the military, as far as I understand, or do you include?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will include everyone, Mr. President: Women, men, military, elderly, everyone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I don't recollect how many there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if I give you the number of 40.000, more or less, do you think that that is approximately the truth?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am just trying to remember where they were in the city. That seems to me high, but there were certainly thousands, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see a reason why a military chief would decide to destroy a city where there are 40.000 of his own citizens?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: His shelling didn't land in their area, sir. The Serbian shelling did not land in the area that I know the Serbs to have been in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thought that you indicated that the shelling was random.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, towards the centre of the city, and it fell outside that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said, sir, that the shelling was indiscriminate. Could you tell us precisely where were the HQs of the brigades, the HQs of battalions and the HQs of companies?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: On which side, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, sir, how can you say that shelling was indiscriminate if you did not know where -- when there was a shell landing, how could you tell if you didn't know whether there was an HQ in that area?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because, sir, I was involved on several occasions trying to negotiate a ceasefire because shells were specifically hitting the UNMOs and civilian only areas, those comments from my counterparts, the UNMOs in the city, and I also witnessed in the area of Rajlovac and the PTT, shells falling in civilian areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, how could you be certain that there were no military targets, mobile military targets, in a place where a shell was landing or was fired at?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no way to be sure, sir, but mobile military targets aren't hit by artillery. It is an inappropriate weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is perhaps an inappropriate weapon, but did you know that in Sarajevo there were possibilities of mechanised transport with mortars which allowed them to be moved around the city?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wheeled transports, and I only make that this distinction because mechanised for me is armoured track vehicles, but, yes, sir, on wheels.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you indicated that you would finish in five minutes. I don't mind if you continue, but it is time from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So Ms. Pilipovic will have less time, and you could not have possibly thought that from the questions I heard until now that you would have finished that in five minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but the matters evolve sometimes very rapidly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The very last question from me. Sir, when you had these meetings with Major Indjic -- I withdraw that. When you had meetings with General Galic, is it true to say that you were not able to speak directly to him because you do not speak Serbian?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Sir, therefore, you had to use an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you always have the same interpreter?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Primarily, yes, sir, in the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, who was the interpreter during these meetings or this meeting with General Galic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely Jadranka, a UN employee. Specifically, I don't know, but most likely Jadranka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This employee, do you know, sir, what was her religion?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Her ethnicity was Serbian, sir. Religion, I am sorry, I don't know, but, ethnicity, she was from Belgrade, if I answered your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it true that you gave a written statement on the 22nd of July, 2000, to Mr. Barry Hogan?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I check my notes?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in this statement, this written statement, you referred to this meeting of the 16th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to review the document, sir. Yes, I see on page 4, a passage there, that refers to the 16th of December, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. On page 4, it starts: "The first time was on 16 December, 1992, with Lieutenant-Colonel Mole. We discussed a corridor for civilians to get out of Sarajevo. He was very hard-nosed in his demand that a corridor be ensured for Serb civilians. He stated that he would open a corridor by fire, if necessary. I knew that he was the commander of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. His staff had told me who he was. I didn't have ready access to him since he was at a rank above which I would usually deal. This meeting lasted about half an hour but no agreement was reached." End of paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this quote, sir. Now, this document that you just read from and that you signed - and we agree that this was on the date that I told you a moment ago, that 2nd of July, 2000 - is it true in this document dated the 2nd of July, 2000, and in relation to this event of the 16th of December, 1992, you never mentioned -- you never mentioned what you told us today in relation to what General Galic allegedly told you with regard to the destruction of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the city and the people inside? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, it is less than two years when you gave a detailed description to the investigators about what went on, and it did not include what you told us this morning or the day before. What happened in the meantime so that we have such a radical change of your position and, I could also say, unexpected change?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several things, sir. When I was notified that I might come to testify and after this written statement was given, I reviewed every document I had. I had not done that prior to giving the statement on 2 July --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to interrupt you, sir. At the end of this statement of the 2nd of July, 1992, there is a text which is prepared by the Prosecution which is called "Witness Acknowledgment," and it says that you can be called to testify before -- in public, before the Tribunal. Didn't you see this addendum, this acknowledgment?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President. Mr. President, my learned colleague has gone to the trouble to ask the witness a question in careful language. The witness has started to answer that question, and he has then been cut off. In my respectful submission, it is not appropriate for counsel to cut off a witness when patently the witness is, indeed, answering the question asked. And once the question is asked, the counsel is obliged to let the witness finish the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the objection is sustained. You started answering several things: "When I was notified I might come to testify and after this written statement was given, I reviewed every document I had. I had not done that prior to giving the statement on the 2nd of July." Could you please complete your answer to this question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The documents that I spoke primarily from on the 2nd of July were my specific diary entries from here. I also, as you see, have a brown book, several reports, and perhaps most importantly approximately 20 hours of video diary. I reviewed all of that in significant detail several times shortly after this document and, in fact, prepared an edited version of the video in perhaps three hours. I developed the map we have used earlier and provided additional written information following the statement here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, thank you for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just interrupt, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. You talked about preparing a summary of the video, and you went in full detail through your notes. Was it your own initiative that you did so? Were you assisted by anyone while doing so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was assisted by a Canadian Forces video technician because I -- as we saw with my camera, I am not very good with electronics, but reviewing the notes was on my own initiative. The development of the map and the editing of the video was something I had offered to Mr. Hogan and offered to do it after his visit in July of 2000. He accepted that, and so I did that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was the office in the OTP in every way assisting you in performing what you intended to do already, or did you just do it on your own with the technical assistance of the person you just spoke about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just by myself, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, sir. If I understand correctly, it was following the fact that you got hold of your documents and suddenly you remembered -- you recalled what General Galic told you and what Commander Indjic told you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I recalled more details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you tell us, please, what are the written documents that you based yourself on in order to claim what you just said?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: This book, sir, is what I call an "O-group book." It is all of the professional notes of meetings with my own staff and colleagues, some observations. Likewise, I had copies of reports from Sarajevo called the "End Month Senior UNMO Reports," dozen of pages which I also reviewed, and other documents that we've referred to here, like the report on Blazuj Hospital, force commanders, commendation, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, am I to conclude from what you just said that this book that you have before you, you used this in order to compile a text which is in italics and in brackets that we saw in the previous document this morning?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially, yes, sir. I also used the video and others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other written documents that you were helped by?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All of the documents that you were able to get a hold of?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of the documents I had, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come that in the document that I quoted earlier, which is your diary including the addenda that you included, it was never mentioned the words of General Galic that he allegedly said and that you testified about or words of Major Indjic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you the author of this document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan's document or the July 2000 document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. The document that was written in July that I quoted this morning.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, sir. I am not sure which document you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We quoted many passages this morning, sir, and it seems that this was your own compilation of your diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether it is a translation confusion or not, but my learned colleague has described -- has referred to a document that was written in July that I quoted this morning. I assume that my friend refers to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. 2nd of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... We are talking about at this very moment. And the question was whether you were the author of that document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am the author of the diary transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you confirm, then, that this date, 2nd of October, 2000, in this document that I partially quoted this morning, anywhere in this document there is no mention whatsoever either to what Major Indjic had allegedly said or what General Galic had allegedly said?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that to be correct, sir. There are indications; but verbatim, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you perhaps indicate for me in this document what are these places where you had written what General Galic had said or Major Indjic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. They are not written, as I meant to say. They are specified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then they are not mentioned in this document dated 2nd of October, 2000; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their text, their words are not mentioned. But 2nd October, 2000, I am sorry, I don't know which one you mean. This document, my diary, is not dated 2nd October, 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, sir. But the covering letter that you addressed at the time to Mr. Barry Hogan, investigator, is dated 2nd of October, 2000. And on the back, we have these pages before you that are reproduced in your diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have an unmarked copy of that exhibit which is P646, if you think it appropriate for the witness to look at it. That is the diary with the covering letter in the format for the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would this assist you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to have this shown to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With great pleasure, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, on the basis of this document -- is this your document? Did you write it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where is it that you wrote the words that were allegedly spoken by General Galic or Major Indjic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I doubt that they appear in this letter, sir. I haven't read it recently, but I doubt that they appear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following this letter, do you have 29 pages that are reproduced in your diary?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it appears so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you indicate for us in these 29 pages where is it that you may have mentioned clearly what General Galic said or what Major Indjic said?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe it is mentioned clearly, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us why not, if that was vital?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This document, I believe -- this document was written directly from my written journal only. The start of this document does say that eventually I will incorporate the video document and other documents that I have completely into this document. That was not done at the time of writing the diary or transcribing the diary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you often spoke about this video. Could you tell us that each time there would be a videotape where General Galic is saying -- talking about his desire that he would raze the city to the ground and rid it of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not of General Galic, sir, I don't have any videotape of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about General Galic.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. It is only me on the video, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, sir. Now, sir, do you know about a book that was written by one of your compatriots called, I believe, "The Lion, the Fox and the Eagle."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am aware. I have it at home. I haven't read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You haven't read it, but you have it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know more or less its contents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK HENNEBERRY [Resumed]
